question:
Write the weekly leadership briefing for the week starting 2025-06-23.
The KPI table was already looked up for you (do not re-query it):
- Revenue: $12,388, vs last week +6.2%, vs 4-week average -82.6%
- Margin: $6,879, vs last week +6.5%, vs 4-week average -77.7%
- Margin %: 55.5%, vs last week +0.1 pts, vs 4-week average +3.0 pts
- Units sold: 504, vs last week -2.3%, vs 4-week average -16.4%
- Orders: 211, vs last week -5.4%, vs 4-week average -19.3%

Investigate with your tools:
1. detect_anomalies for revenue and margin_pct with period "2025-Q2": grain "week" with by "total",
   and grain "month" with by "channel" and by "territory" (reseller orders arrive about once a
   month, so weekly checks by channel or territory raise false alarms).
2. run_sql to find out WHY the biggest change happened (channel, territory, category, discount).
3. make_chart once or twice (e.g. weekly revenue by channel for the last 13 weeks as a bar chart;
   Reseller orders arrive about monthly, so a line would mislead).

Only give a reason if a tool result shows it; otherwise say it needs checking. No forecasts.
Reply in EXACTLY this format (every number from a tool result or the table):
HEADLINE: <one sentence>
WHAT CHANGED AND WHY:
- <2-3 bullets>
WATCH LIST:
- <1-3 bullets, one per unusual run found, with dates and numbers>
FOLLOW-UPS:
- <2-3 recommended actions or questions for the team>
answer:
HEADLINE: Week starting 2025-06-23 was a modest rebound in revenue and margin, but the quarter still shows a sharp disruption from late April through June, driven mainly by channel and territory swings.

WHAT CHANGED AND WHY:
- Revenue was $12,388 and margin was $6,879, both up vs last week (+6.2% and +6.5%), while margin % held at 55.5% (+0.1 pts); units fell to 504 (-2.3%) and orders to 211 (-5.4%).
- The biggest change in the quarter was the collapse in Reseller activity: anomaly checks flagged no Reseller sales in 2025-05 and 2025-06, and the weekly channel chart shows Reseller revenue was $3,416,763.86 on 2025-04-28 before dropping to near-zero levels afterward.
- Territory checks also show the disruption was broad: Germany, Southwest, United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada all had unusual low runs in May/June, while some territories had unusually high margin % in the same period; the exact operational cause needs checking in the underlying business process.

WATCH LIST:
- Revenue anomaly: 2025-04-28 was a high outlier for total revenue at $3,791,016, followed by a low run from 2025-05-26 to 2025-06-16 with a peak of only $11,031.
- Margin % anomaly: 2025-04-28 was a low outlier at 3.7%, then 2025-06-02 to 2025-06-23 was unusually high with a peak of 56.9%.
- Channel/territory anomalies: Reseller had no sales in 2025-05 and 2025-06; Central and Northeast had no sales at all in 2025-06.

FOLLOW-UPS:
- Check whether the Reseller channel had a data, fulfillment, or booking issue in May and June, since the anomaly is large and persistent.
- Review territory coverage for Central and Northeast in June to confirm whether the missing sales are expected or a reporting gap.
- Investigate the late-April spike and margin dip on 2025-04-28 to see which orders, products, or discounts created the swing.

Checked with: q19, q20, q21, q22, q23, chart_7

periods.note: 'Last year' means 2024. 'Last quarter' means 2025-Q2 (data stops on 2025-06-29, so it is missing its last 1 day(s); say so).

dictionary.dialect: SQLite. Use strftime() for dates, LIMIT (not TOP), || to join text. Read-only.

main_view.name: sales_lines
main_view.grain: one row per order line (one product on one sales order)

columns.week_start: Monday of the order's week, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.territory: sales territory: Northwest, Northeast, Central, Southwest, Southeast, Canada, France, Germany, Australia, United Kingdom
columns.country: country code (US, CA, FR, DE, AU, GB)
columns.revenue: LineTotal: money for the line after discount

dictionary.raw_tables: SalesOrderHeader, SalesOrderDetail, Product, ProductSubcategory, ProductCategory, SalesTerritory, Customer (Microsoft's original column names). Prefer sales_lines.
caveats: standard_cost is today's cost for each product, not the cost at the time of the order.
The first month (2022-05) only has a few days of data.
